# web3os.space

> web3os.space is a shared operating system that runs on many ordinary computers: storage first, then applications, computing power and AI, paid in one coin (WEB3OS) on its own chain, Web3OSChain. This file is the entry point for AI coding assistants that build web3os.space applications for a person.

An application is a folder of static front-end files plus a manifest (name, services, scopes, author share). Both are published to the network and a registered name points at the manifest. The user's own node resolves the name, checks the user's grant and serves the front end into a sandboxed frame: CSP `default-src 'self'; connect-src 'none'; sandbox allow-scripts`, so no fetch, XHR or WebSocket and no shared storage. The only way out is `postMessage` to the host, which the SDK wraps; the node decides every call. Keep application logic in a pure module with no clock and no randomness, and test it with `node --test`, passing a fake window as the last argument of each SDK call.

Rules an assistant must follow: use only the calls, scopes and refusal codes in the reference; handle every refusal code as the reference says (retry, ask the user, or fix the application); never ask the user for recovery words or keys; spend only through the SDK's payment calls, which stay within the allowance the user set in the host.

Status: the guide and the reference are public. The developer kit (SDK file, sample application, local test node) is published when the remaining application interfaces land; until then, paths in the guide such as `Apps/` and `Scripts/testnet/` refer to that kit.

## Docs

- [Developer guide](https://web3os.space/developers/guide.md): what an application is, sandbox rules, manifest and scopes, sign-in, content and streams, payments, messaging, refusals, publishing, the model-test loop
- [SDK reference](https://web3os.space/developers/reference.md): the generated tables of calls, scopes and refusal codes
